"''No, no, no. Do not put any more stuff on that part of the desk. That's my work area.''"
[The droid beeps again]|quotestart=0|quoteend=0|Colonel Tuttle|}} Around [[9 ABY]], an [[R-series]] [[astromech droid]] served as a '''mail droid''' at a [[New Republic]] [[New Republic Coruscant skyscraper (Tuttle's office)|skyscraper]] on the [[planet]] [[Coruscant]]. At one point around that [[Standard year|year]], the [[droid]] bumped into a New Republic [[Unidentified lab tech|archival office employee]] while transporting a caddy of [[datacard]]s, which the archival worker [[Penn Pershing]] then took. Later, the droid delivered another set of datacards to the [[Tuttle's office|office]] of [[Requisitions]] [[Colonel]] [[Tuttle]], where it deposited it on his desk despite the colonel's protests. ==Biography== {{Quote|It's okay. He can stay. You, scoot.''"
[The mail droid beeps]|quoteend=0|Colonel Tuttle, acknowledging the visit of Captain Carson Teva and dismissing the mail droid|}} Around [[9 ABY]],{{MandoDate|21}} an [[astromech droid]] worked as a mail [[droid]] in a [[New Republic Coruscant skyscraper (Tuttle's office)|skyscraper]] of the [[New Republic]] located on the [[Core Worlds]] [[planet]]''[[Star Wars: Galactic Atlas: Updated Edition]]'' [[Coruscant]]. At one point around that [[Standard year|year]], the droid was transporting a caddy of [[datacard]]s in an [[Congenial Archive|archival office]]. There, an [[Unidentified lab tech|employee]] of the office was talking with the [[New Republic Amnesty Program|Amnesty Program]] member [[Penn Pershing]], who was archiving records of [[Galactic Empire]] technology scheduled for destruction, at the latter's cubicle. The mail droid bumped into the former worker, who was standing in{{TheMandalorian|Chapter 19: The Convert}} its way, and warbled. Pershing then excused himself and took the caddy from the droid—who made more warbling noises—stating that he was falling behind in his work. At that point, the droid moved away from the cubicle. [[File:DontYouDare-Chapter21ThePirate.png|thumb|right|320px|The mail droid directly ignored a request by Colonel Tuttle.]] Later around that same year, the droid was present in the [[Tuttle's office|office]] of [[Colonel]] [[Tuttle]] of [[Requisitions]]. While the colonel was working on several caddies of datacards near his office's [[Viewport|window]], the droid approached Tuttle's cluttered desk while carrying another caddy, and the colonel spoke to the droid. The mail droid beeped and moved to deposit the caddy on the desk, only for Tuttle to forbid it, claiming the free area of the desk in question was his "work area." While looking at the colonel, the mail droid nevertheless deposited its caddy on the desk and beeped again, to Tuttle's shocked expression. Furthermore, the droid then pushed at the caddy it had put on the desk and made more noises, to which the colonel changed his face to that of annoyance and shook his head. At that point, [[New Republic Defense Force]] [[Captain]] [[Carson Teva]], who had arrived on Coruscant in order to request authorization and backup for driving off a [[Pirate siege on Nevarro|pirate siege]] on the [[Outer Rim Territories]] planet [[Nevarro]], entered into Tuttle's office, accompanied by Tuttle's [[Unidentified Rodian assistant|assistant]], who was attempting to stop the captain from disturbing the colonel with his unscheduled visit. While the mail droid was still present in the office, the [[Aide|assistant]] apologized to Tuttle for the disturbance. In response, the colonel agreed to see Teva and then pointed to the droid and jerked his [[Limb|finger]] at the office's door, ordering the droid to "scoot." At that, the mail droid beeped again, and both the assistant and the droid subsequently left Tuttle's office. ==Characteristics== The mail droid was an [[R-series]] astromech droid manufactured by [[Industrial Automaton]]. It had the head of an [[R6 astromech droid|R6 astromech]],{{GEAttr|Droid Depot}} [[Color|white]]-and-yellow-colored plating, and a black [[photoreceptor]]. The droid had a penchant for ignoring the convenience of its organic co-workers, directly going against the request of Colonel Tuttle as well as bumping into an archival office employee standing in its way. ==Equipment== The mail droid was outfitted with a tray that could be used for carrying caddies of datacards. ==Behind the scenes== The mail droid first appeared in "[[Chapter 19: The Convert]]," the third episode of the [[Disney+]] television show ''[[Star Wars: The Mandalorian]]''{{'s}} [[The Mandalorian Season Three|third season]]. The episode aired on [[March 15]], [[2023]].{{D23|url=everything-new-you-can-stream-on-disney-in-march-2023|text=Everything New You Can Stream on Disney+ in March 2023}} The droid's paint scheme is similar to that of [[R6-D8]],''[[Star Wars: The Rise of Skywalker: The Visual Dictionary]]'' a droid featured in the [[2019]] [[sequel trilogy]] film, [[Star Wars: Episode IX The Rise of Skywalker|''Star Wars'': Episode IX ''The Rise of Skywalker'']].{{Film|IX}} ==Appearances== {{Indexpage}} {{Mediacat|imagecat=Images of the unidentified mail droid}} *[[The Mandalorian – The Graphic Novel of Season 3|''The Mandalorian'' – The Graphic Novel of Season 3]] *{{TheMandalorian|Chapter 19: The Convert}} {{1st}} *{{TheMandalorian|Chapter 21: The Pirate}} ==Sources== *''[[Star Wars Encyclopedia: The Comprehensive Guide to the Star Wars Galaxy]]'' {{Imo}} ==Notes and references== {{Reflist}} {{Interlang |ka=უცნობი ფოსტალიონი დროიდი }} [[Category:Droids of the New Republic]] [[Category:Droids with it/its pronouns]] [[Category:Droids with unspecified gender programming]] [[Category:R-series astromech droids]]
